steps: Situation: the target skill's output is creative / non-deterministic (for example writing tone or prose).

SKILL.md:84-88 treats this as a case where the gate cannot run; report the blocker and suggest skill-tuning. SKILL.md:358-360 lists it as a do-NOT-invoke case because the equivalence check is unreliable.
references/equivalence-check-protocol.md:119-122 says for the same output class that the skill self-aborts and recommends skill-tuning.
references/multi-judge-ensemble.md:165-166 says that for the same output class the agent must run the full ensemble.
The agent cannot both self-abort before Q1 and run the full Q1 ensemble on that target.
findings.why: When a target skill's output is non-deterministic or creative, one file requires running the full judge ensemble while SKILL.md and the equivalence protocol require aborting and routing to skill-tuning.

side_b.quote: Token count delta is suspiciously large (>30% reduction in

steps: Situation: a candidate's output is more than 30% shorter than baseline.
equivalence-check-protocol.md:21 and :23 make output token count within ±20% a required Layer 1 check; failure means REJECT immediately, without Layer 2.
equivalence-check-protocol.md:85 and :89-91 treat a >30% output reduction as a state that can occur 'Even if both layers pass' and only mark it suspicious.
A >30% reduction cannot pass the ±20% check, so the same quantity has two limits with different consequences: rejection beyond 20%, suspicion beyond 30%.
findings.why: For the output token delta on a candidate, the same file sets a hard ±20% pass limit and also describes a >30% reduction as coexisting with a Layer 1 pass, which the first limit makes impossible.

side_a.quote: In that case, Layer 1 pass = PROCEED.

steps: Situation: a deterministic target and a Low-risk move, where multi-judge-ensemble.md:154-160 permits skipping the ensemble.
The agent runs Layer 1 only, and it passes; multi-judge-ensemble.md:162 assigns PROCEED.

SKILL.md:106-107 makes the Q1 pass rule 'structural OK and PASS_HIGH or PASS_MODERATE', and with no ensemble there is no such result, so the skipped-ensemble carve-out is not reflected in SKILL.md's Q1 rule.

Independently of Q1, SKILL.md:92-93 and :155-158 reserve PROCEED for rounds where Q1, Q2 and Q3 all pass, and SKILL.md:128 rejects a <5% reduction. Suppose that same round has a <5% reduction: Layer 1 pass = PROCEED but Q2 = REJECT.
The skip clause states an exception to running the ensemble, but it does not state an exception to Q2 or Q3, so the verdict conflict remains.
findings.why: On a structural-only round whose Layer 1 passes but whose Q2 or Q3 fails, the ensemble reference assigns PROCEED while SKILL.md requires all three checks to pass and otherwise REJECT.

side_a.quote: **Input**: User says "let me try this rewording — it's clearer".

side_b.quote: | Reword for "clarity" with judgment call | Taste, not refactor | `skill-tuning` |

steps: Situation: the user proposes a rewording because it is clearer.
SKILL.md:309-327 handles this input inside the skill: it runs Q1, Q2 and Q3, holds on FLAG_TIER_2, then rejects the round. SKILL.md:329-331 presents this as what the ensemble is for.

references/refactor-moves-catalog.md:185 and :187 say out-of-scope moves are not to be done in refactor and must be routed elsewhere if proposed; line 194 sends a clarity rewording with a judgment call to skill-tuning.
The agent cannot both route the proposal away as out of scope and process it through the refactor gate in this skill.
findings.why: For a user-proposed 'clearer' rewording, the catalog requires routing to skill-tuning without doing it in refactor, while SKILL.md's worked example runs that same proposal through the refactor gate.

side_b.quote: | Skill has no `test-prompts.json` and user is unwilling to write any | The gate cannot run; revert to `skill-creator-advance` |

steps: Situation: the target has no test-prompts.json and the user will not write one, so baseline item (1) from SKILL.md:49-52 cannot be obtained.
SKILL.md:84-88 covers any of items (1)-(4) being unobtainable: suggest skill-tuning for a quality intent, or manual edit for a cosmetic one.
SKILL.md:246 gives a different destination for the same blocker: revert to skill-creator-advance. SKILL.md:355-357 repeats that destination.

references/test-prompts-schema.md:135-137 also says skill-tuning self-aborts with fewer than 3 prompts, so the skill-tuning suggestion from line 87 cannot complete under this condition unless the user supplies prompts.
findings.why: When test prompts are absent and the user refuses to write them, SKILL.md gives two different exits, skill-tuning or manual edit versus skill-creator-advance, and the skill-tuning exit self-aborts under the same condition.

side_a.quote: Accept the output as-is if it's truly good

side_b.quote: | Goldens that look identical to current skill output | Adds no information; just baseline-locks |

steps: Situation: during golden curation, the current skill's output on a representative prompt is truly good.
golden-anchor-protocol.md:106-109 runs the current best version and directs accepting that output as-is.
The saved golden (line 113) is then identical to current skill output.
golden-anchor-protocol.md:187-192 lists goldens identical to current skill output as an anti-pattern.
findings.why: When the current output is good and is accepted as-is, the curation process yields exactly the golden the same file names as an anti-pattern; the conflict is uncertain only because the process also offers editing or rewriting options.

side_a.quote: record that acceptance as `PROCEED` before applying it.

side_b.quote: win; it does not auto-advance the ratchet.

steps: Situation: a package-mode candidate has a 5-10% whole-package reduction, passes the other gates, and the user accepts the marginal win.
references/package-resource-mode.md:15 yields RESHAPE, and :77-79 requires recording the acceptance as PROCEED before applying it.
SKILL.md:157-158 defines PROCEED as all three checks passing strictly, followed by git commit, and states 'ratchet advances'. A literal PROCEED record therefore advances the ratchet.
SKILL.md:41-42 says a 5-10% reduction does not auto-advance the ratchet, and SKILL.md:131-132 says the 10% threshold prevents accumulating ratchet credit from micro-edits.
The result is incompatible if 'does not auto-advance' applies after user acceptance; it is compatible only if 'auto' means solely 'without user acceptance', which is why confidence is low.
findings.why: On an accepted 5-10% package-mode candidate, recording PROCEED brings the verdict definition 'ratchet advances' into conflict with the rule that a marginal reduction does not advance the ratchet automatically.
